claims.text: The proposed intervention is to train a machine-learning potential on ab initio data specific to the high-entropy-alloy compositions being studied.
The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states.
The proposed scope is restricted to alloys containing at least five principal elements.
The applicable temperatures are close to the alloys' melting points.
A composition-specific machine-learning potential can capture complex atomic interactions and configurations in these alloys.
The machine-learning potential will represent the potential-energy surface more accurately than the EAM reference.
A more accurate potential-energy surface will allow better sampling of liquid-state configurations.
Better sampling of liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will improve the accuracy of free-energy calculations.
TOR-TILD currently uses EAM references for high-entropy alloys.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on alloy composition and machine-learning-model quality.
Failure to obtain a significant mismatch reduction relative to EAM for the same alloy and temperature would falsify the hypothesis.
